title: Provenance-first analytics reingest with incremental schema migration
creator: Maya Bennett
description:
Background: The Console analytics event schema has evolved multiple times over the past 18 months. Historical events stored in raw S3 partitions cannot be reliably joined against new downstream consumers without on-the-fly transforms. Current ad-hoc backfills reapply minimal transforms and frequently require manual corrections (see ENG-9473 and ENG-40288).

Goal: Provide a provenance-first reingestion pipeline that can apply incremental schema migrations to historical events during backfill runs while preserving event lineage, enabling idempotent retries, and producing a verifiable output that downstream metrics and dashboards can consume. This should allow team-level backfills (per-customer or per-product), wide-range replays (date windows), and one-off fixes without impacting live ingestion.

Scope:
- Implement provenance metadata tagging for every reingested event (origin-run-id, source-partition, original-offset, transform-version).
- Build schema-migration hooks that run in a deterministic order and are versioned (migration-1.0, migration-1.1...). Hooks must be reversible where feasible and have safety checks.
- Provide an idempotent replay executor that uses event UUID + provenance token to avoid duplicate downstream writes.
- Support predicate-based selective reingest (filter by customer_id, route, or event type) to reduce blast radius and cost.
- Add checkpointed run state persisted in the backfill service to resume on failure and to enable partial cancel/resume.
- Provide validation and diff harness to compare before/after metrics (event counts, embeddings production, function-calls surfaced) and a canary rollout path.

Design highlights:
- Staging: reingest runner streams raw events from historical S3 into a staging Kafka topic with provenance headers. Staging topic uses compacted partitions keyed by event_uuid to surface latest migrated payload.
- Transform layer: run migration hooks as containerized workers that read from staging topic and emit to an output topic. Hooks are composed and versioned; each hook annotates the transform-version header.
- Dedup & idempotency: downstream writers use (event_uuid, origin-run-id) as a unique key. Duplicate detection happens at write-time in the sink (BigQuery/ClickHouse) using upsert semantics or at an idempotency service layer for write-once targets.
- Checkpointing: run state is persisted to the backfill-service DB (Postgres) with fine-grained per-partition/offset checkpoints and provenance tokens for traceability.
- Canary + validation: run a small scoped canary (1% customers or single product-area) and compare a set of golden metrics and a hashed sample of transformed payloads. The validation harness will publish diffs to a verification dashboard.

Trade-offs considered:
- On-the-fly transforms vs. materializing migrated historical datasets: on-the-fly reduces storage but increases compute and complexity. We opt for hybrid: materialize only when downstream consumers require stable historical joins (configurable).
- Using compacted Kafka staging increases operational burden but gives us a single source-of-truth for mutated historical events and simplifies resume semantics.
- Dedupe at sink adds latency for some stores; if latency is unacceptable, we will use a short-lived idempotency cache in front of the sink.

Runbook & rollout:
- Phase 1 (dev): implement staging topic, provenance headers, and simple migration hook scaffold. Unit tests for determinism and idempotency. (ENG-118206)
- Phase 2 (internal canary): run per-product small-scale reingest and wire verification dashboard. Add cost telemetry. (ENG-118207)
- Phase 3 (wider backfill): provide guarded self-serve backfill API in Console, with ACLs and billing estimation. (ENG-118208)

Observability & SLOs:
- Key metrics: reingest throughput (events/s), transform CPU time, canary pass-rate, validation diffs, rollback frequency.
- Alerts: stalled checkpoints > 15 min, canary diff > 1% of event_fields, runaway retry > 5x baseline.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ANALYTICS/Provenance+Reingest+Design (draft)
- Verification dashboard (prototype): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/analytics/reingest-verification
- Initial PR (scaffold): https://github.com/redwood-inference/replay-runner/pull/472

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Run a scoped reingest for a single product area and produce migrated events with provenance headers.
Checkpointing allows resuming a run from the last persisted offset without duplicating writes.
Validation harness can detect payload diffs for a sampled subset and report pass/fail to the verification dashboard.
Idempotency guarantees: reingest of same date-range/run-id does not create duplicate downstream rows.
Selective predicate reingest (customer_id or event_type) completes within the expected cost envelope and has documented API in Console.
design_notes: Use compacted Kafka staging topic keyed by event_uuid to serve both dedupe and resume semantics.
Migration hooks should be small, deterministic functions (no external side-effects) and versioned via semantic tags.
Persist run metadata and checkpoints in Postgres with JSONB for provenance tokens; ensure indices for resume queries.
Provide an SDK for writing migration hooks (python/ts) to reduce friction for product owners.
Backfill cost estimator will run a sampling pass to estimate compute and egress before user-triggered backfills.
risks: Large-scale reingests may exceed GPU/CPU quotas and increase cost; need hard limits and preflight estimation.
Transform non-determinism (e.g., reliance on external APIs) could cause drift; enforce deterministic-only hooks via CI checks.
Privacy/regulatory: some historical events may contain PII; ensure transformations and retention comply with customer data policies.
Operational complexity: compacted topics and checkpointing increases SRE burden for disaster recovery.
